Okay, please try it now (version 0.25). I think I've fixed the problem. And it should work with or without git-bash. There might still be some other issue downstream, but I _think_ this is it.

_If you're curious: There's one place where I'm using `path.join()` to construct a URL. It worked fine in Mac / Linux, but in Windows it was changing "http://" to "http:/". I added an ugly regex to fix it for now. Will go back when I get a chance and clean up that code._

issue.title: fix broken URLs on the start page in Windows

repository.name: api-simulator
repository.description: Turn an OpenAPI spec into a local API in one command. Build and test your frontend with custom responses, shared state, and simulated failures, without waiting for the backend.

events.body: Can you elaborate here? Are you saying if the OpenApi spec is missing a prefix you want Counterfact to add it?

I haven't given this much thought. But as I understand it OpenAPI is relative to some basepath.

In most cases this basepath is just the domain

`https://myfancyapi.com/`

But in some cases it could be relevant to a prefixed url

`https://bigcorp.com/employeeGateway/`

As I understand it openAPI will not mention this `employeeGateway `in any way, all paths are just appended to the end of the url.

For Counterfact, the basepath is by defauly `localhost:3100` so our paths will be added to it. Say our internal api paths are `/api/person/1` the resulting url will be `http://localhost:3100/api/person/1`

When I start up Counterfact I can add a prefix, using `--prefix` So if I add /employeeGateway Counterfact is available at 

`http://localhost:3100/employeeGateway/api/person/1`

This will ensure that I can more easily change from a production and mock api on a running client.

However if I go into Swagger and try out I get 404 because swagger tries out the normal path.

A recent PR updated CF to support the `basePath`: https://github.com/pmcelhaney/counterfact/pull/797

So now if your spec has a `basePath` included, and if your client includes that path in its requests, Counterfact will silently handle it correctly. Let me know if that meets this need.

> This will ensure that I can more easily change from a production and mock api on a running client.

There's a better way. You can have Counterfact proxy to the production server. You can then switch between mocks and the proxy to production at runtime. The client code doesn't need a mechanism to switch back and forth at runtime.  

I have big plans to build on this feature. You'll be able to have some endpoints point to production while others are mocked. You'll be able to flip the switch at runtime through a GUI that also serves as an alternative to Postman or Swagger UI which is easier to use. 

I'm typing on my phone so I can't easily link to the docs, but please let me know if that makes sense and fits your use case.
@IngoVals What do you think? Do you still have concerns or can we close this issue?

What about the prefix attribute in Counterfact, if the plan is to support that still you could just try it out. Run counterfact, with a prefix, open up the swagger endpoint, and try to run an endpoint.

Unless I'm missing something this will not work, which is probably not what we want.

You're right! I forgot that before the OpenAPI doc is passed to Swagger, a URL is injected into the servers object.

https://github.com/pmcelhaney/counterfact/blob/291beab83e53da2c3e8bae0177b829ed516bf5a8/src/server/openapi-middleware.ts#L19-L22

That URL should include the prefix, which is stored as `config.routePrefix`. If we add a routePrefix argument to the `openApiMiddlware()` function and pass in `config.routePrefix` from [create-koa-app.ts](https://github.com/pmcelhaney/counterfact/blob/main/src/server/create-koa-app.ts#L23), we can append the prefix to the `url` in the above code snippet. 

Note that the type of the `Config` object is missing `routePrefix`, a mistake that needs to be corrected.
Can you create a minimal test case?
Well, I stripped my OpenApi doc down to just the failing endpoint and it works fine. Digging in further to find out why it fails as part of the larger set and then I'll report back.

Ok, I have it now. Use the attached open spec. There is a single endpoint starting with MyCompanies. If you run the swagger UI execute function it will work correctly. However, if you execute the command as a cURL call and change the case of the path it fails. Note the call below where `MyCompanies` is written as `myCompanies`.

```
curl -X 'GET' \
  'http://localhost:3100/myCompanies/4817/Accounts?type=createDomestic' \
  -H 'accept: application/json'
```

The Counterfact `dispatcher` assumes an exact match in the `operationForPathAndMethod` function so when it looked for `/myCompanies/{id}/Accounts` it found no match, but if you issue the curl against `/MyCompanies/{id}/Accounts` it works just fine.

I realize that case sensitivity in url paths is not consistent on the web. Windows servers such as IIS are case insensitive but often other platforms would consider `/MyCompanies` and `/myCompanies` as different paths. So I'm not sure what CF should do here. From what I've researched it seems most REST API developers recommend assuming your paths are case insensitive so that a server won't really care about casing. That helps for users who might enter the wrong case.

I recommend we just change `dispatcher` to ignore case when looking in the paths object. I'll put together a PR if that seems good to you.

[openapi-v2.json](https://github.com/pmcelhaney/counterfact/files/14865449/openapi-v2.json)

I know we've chatted about case sensitivity before. I think it's better to be conservative by default and assume production will be case sensitive. 

But I'm not opposed to an option that turns off case sensitivity.

I agree that we should be conservative by default. I'm going to go ahead and add a PR to add the option since it is a valid use case and we can't always ask the upstream consumers of an API to change their call points.

Actually, the real place in `module-tree` is line 75 and following where it adds the segment to the directory as lower case:
```
this.addModuleToDirectory(
      directory.directories[segment.toLocaleLowerCase()],
      remainingSegments,
      module,
    );
```
Given the above I think we just drop the idea of an input option and just make `dispatcher` not care about case.

To aid discussion, I added a PR that just updates the logic without the new option for ignoring case. This just brings `dispatcher` into line with the already case-insensitive matching of the `Registry`

Thanks. In theory we should trace dependencies and reload only the affected files. But since restarting is so fast I'm going to try reloading all of the files, no matter which one changed. That should solve the problem. 

When Node officially supports VM modules I'll do it the "right" way.
Working on this now. I'm not sure if I'll have time this weekend, but it should be fixed by April 21 at the latest.

issue.title: reload everything when a file changes

repository.name: api-simulator
repository.description: Turn an OpenAPI spec into a local API in one command. Build and test your frontend with custom responses, shared state, and simulated failures, without waiting for the backend.

issue.body:
Fixes #835 

When any file is touched, the entire app is reloaded. This is necessary because any file that imports the file that was changed (directly or indirectly) needs to be reloaded.

I'm a bit concerned this is going to cause performance problems on large codebases, but we'll see. Ideally, instead of reloading everything, we would trace dependencies and only reload the files that need to be reloaded.

events.body: Almost there. I just want to make sure the server pauses while things are loading so we don't have any race conditions.

It looks like we're going to have to trace dependencies and only reload the affected files. Otherwise the refresh will take too long for large codebases.

I don't think tracing dependencies will be particularly hard, it's just going to take a bit more time to implement.
Most of the code for tracing dependencies is done, so I should have this wrapped up in a few days.

Finished the code to trace dependencies. It's not working because imports are cached. In other words if we have a file that contains:

```ts
import { x } from "./x.js";
```

Then if we change `x.js` and reload the file, Node will use the original copy of `x.js`. And there's no way to invalidate the cache. 

I can think of three ways to possibly work around it:

1. Use [child processes](https://devlizioso.substack.com/p/how-to-implement-an-hot-reload-system) somehow.
2. Rewrite imports to a cache-busting query string. 
3. Always compile to CJS so that we can invalidate the cache.

Of these, the third seems like the simplest. Since I figured out a way use `require()` from ESM, and we're already invalidating the cache every time we `require()` an updated file, that might work with very little modification.

<del>Okay, I think this will actually work today as long as your output directory has a `package.json` with `{type: "CommonJS"}`.</del>

Which is fine as long as you're not intending the mock code to be part of a larger package. 

I would rather it "just work" for everyone, so I think what I'm going to have to do is emit ".cjs" files from the transpiler. The transpiler will also have to rewrite references to local ".js" files to ".cjs".

Finally got it working with #879! Will put out a release shortly. 

Thank you for the feedback. This is an important fix.

	package.json
	counterfact/
		path-types/
		paths/
			mocks/ <-- my custom code
				session-manager.ts
			_.context.ts
		package.json

I have a lot of custom code in that `/mocks` directory, but I'm simplifying things here to a minimal test case.

### counterfact/package.json
```json
{
	"name": "my-ui-counterfact",
	"version": "0.0.1",
	"private": true,
	"scripts": {
		"mockapi": "counterfact ../path/to/my/openapi.yaml ."
	},
	"devDependencies": {
		"counterfact": "^0.42.0"
	},
	"type": "commonjs"
}
```

### counterfact/paths/_.context.ts
```ts
import { SessionManager } from './mocks/session-manager';

const sessionManager = new SessionManager();

export class Context {
	someCustomFunction(): any {
		return sessionManager.toString();
	}
}
```

### counterfact/paths/mocks/session-manager.ts
```ts
class SessionManager {}
export { SessionManager };
```

With all that in place, when I run `my-ui/counterfact> npm run mockapi`, I get the following:

Please let me know if my setup is unsupported/I'm doing something wrong, if you cannot reproduce, or if this is a genuine bug.

issue.body:
fixes #890

Don't generate a unique variable name when referencing a variable that is exported. 

This may create a problem if an OpenAPI spec has a component that references two different components that happen to have the same name. But that's probably an edge case that's much more unusual than recursive types, which this change fixes.

events.body: Fixed in 0.40.2. Thank you for the bug report! If you have any other feedback, please don't hesitate to share.

Thanks for letting me know! The issue is Counterfact expects the imported file to have a `.js` extension. 

```ts
import { SessionManager } from './mocks/session-manager';
```

If you add the `.js` extension it should work. 

```ts
import { SessionManager } from './mocks/session-manager.js';
```

Adding the `.js` extension is considered a best practice. I'll link a reference when I find it. However, I don't see any value in being pedantic about it. I'll fix the code so that either no extension, `.js`, or `.ts` works.
Fixed in 0.42.1. Please let me know if that does the trick (and the hot reload works)!

Ah yes, my inexperience with node is showing. Sure enough, I added file extensions and it worked! I see how node (and its module systems) are more browser-like and require full paths to resources (unlike other languages where file extensions are omitted, which was my naive assumption).

I'll stick with explicit extensions, but I'm sure someone out where will appreciate the flexibility.

I tested it out hot reloading, and indeed it works like a charm now! Lightning fast and seamless. Well done.

I consider this issue closed.

Awesome! At this point it should work even without the file extension. Any valid TypeScript code should work. If you run into anything that doesn't work, or behaves in a way that is not obvious, please let me know. I want this tool to be absurdly intuitive.
